notes:
simple-capture is a screen recorder with a light editor. It records the screen, a camera, the microphone and system audio, and exports MP4, MOV, WebM, GIF or animated WebP. Everything happens on the Mac. There is no account, sign-in, server or in-app purchase, and the app makes no network connections, so no demo account is needed.

WHERE TO FIND IT
simple-capture is a menu bar app. Its main entry point is the simple-capture icon in the menu bar (top right of the screen), whose menu has Open Recorder, Library, Diagnostics, About simple-capture and Quit. The recorder window opens by itself on the first launch, and whenever the app is opened again from Finder or Launchpad while it is running. The recorder is a floating panel without a Dock icon; a Dock icon appears only while the editor, Library, Diagnostics or About window is open.

PERMISSIONS
simple-capture checks permissions without prompting. macOS asks only when the user presses Allow, and only for what is used:
- Screen Recording: to list windows and apps and to record the screen and system audio.
- Camera: only when a camera is chosen (Screen + Camera or Camera Only).
- Microphone: only when a microphone is chosen under Audio.

HOW TO TEST (about 2 minutes)
1. The recorder opens on the first launch (later: menu bar icon > Open Recorder). Click the "Permissions needed" banner at the top of the recorder to open the Permissions window.
2. Press Allow… next to Screen Recording. When macOS asks, open System Settings, switch on simple-capture under Privacy & Security > Screen & System Audio Recording, and choose Quit & Reopen. Then open the recorder again from the menu bar icon.
   Without this permission, the System… button under the source list records through Apple's system content picker instead.
3. Optional: choose Screen + Camera at the top and pick a camera, and pick a microphone under Audio. Press Allow… for each in the Permissions window.
4. Under Source > Displays, select a display and press Record. After a 3-second countdown, a small control bar appears; it is left out of the recording. Record for about 10 seconds, then press the stop button in the control bar (or Stop Recording in the menu bar icon's menu).
5. The editor opens with the recording. Press Space to play it. Optionally drag an edge of the clip to trim it, or press T to add text.
6. Press Export… (Command-E), choose MP4 and press Export. The file is saved in Movies/simple-capture.
Menu bar icon > Library… lists every recording.

ENTITLEMENTS
- App Sandbox: settings and logs stay in the app's container.
- Camera: the camera overlay, Camera Only, and a cabled iPhone or iPad, which macOS presents as a capture device.
- Microphone (audio input): the microphone chosen under Audio.
- Movies folder read/write: recordings and exports go to ~/Movies/simple-capture.
- User-selected read/write and app-scope bookmarks: an export folder chosen with Choose… in the Export sheet (kept across launches) and a background image picked in an Open dialog.
- Outgoing network connections (network.client): the windows are WKWebView pages loaded from files inside the app, and WebKit's WebContent and Networking processes need this entitlement in a sandboxed app even for local content. The app itself makes no network connections.

IPHONE AND IPAD
The iPhone tab in the recorder lists an iPhone or iPad connected by USB cable (unlocked, with "Trust This Computer" accepted) and records its screen and sound. It needs a cabled device and can be skipped.

ENCODING HELPERS
Exports are encoded by bundled helpers (sc-ffmpeg and sc-ffprobe in Contents/MacOS) that inherit the app's sandbox, built from FFmpeg under the LGPL 2.1 with network support disabled. H.264 and HEVC use Apple's VideoToolbox. About simple-capture lists the licenses; the FFmpeg entry's Source code button opens the helpers' source code on GitHub.

The privacy policy is linked from the About window and from the App Store listing.
